cells.tense: You are here, pen in hand, keeping the mix right as the weight shifts.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Show someone a thing you were shown how to do — a recipe, a method, a way of saying something — and alter a piece of it as you pass it along.
cells.core:
You can hold a lot and still keep it in tune. When something heavy lands, you feel how much it carries and you move with it — a little more here, a little less there — so whatever you're holding stays whole and the room stays level. That adjusting isn't a trick. It's you, here, working by feel.

What's ready to move through you is something you were given. A way of doing a thing, learned from someone, that still works and could take one change to keep living. Hand it on this week and shift a piece of it as you go — not to improve it, not to fix it, just to let it come through your hands. The version that arrives is yours, and whoever receives it gets something kept, not preserved.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the whole thing in tune while it's in your hands.
cells.verb: adjusting the blend by feel as the weight shifts
cells.place: where the weight and the tuning sit in your hands at once

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future you are already trying to smooth down.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Go after something you want today, not the thing that keeps the table even. A single step, small enough that no one needs to approve it first.
cells.core:
You're running in front of the room. When something is about to go uneven, you're already smoothing it — agreeing sooner than you mean, dropping a distinction because the friction is coming. The weight you carry is real, and you're spending it on harmony nobody asked for. Whatever would have stood up for itself doesn't get the chance.

Underneath, it isn't peace you're after. There's something you want, and you've been going around it to keep things level. Move at it instead. One step today, the way the feeling already leans — not a plan, not a talk, just the step. The evenness you're reaching for comes after you've let one thing stand.
cells.sheetLine: You're making peace before anyone's said the real thing.

cells.place: where the weight and the tuning sit in your hands at once

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Have someone you trust sit with you in something heavy. Don't explain it, don't fix it, don't perform being fine. Just stay with them being there.
cells.core:
You can't find the middle. Contact pulls you off center, and holding much of anything feels like it's slipping. That isn't a flaw in you. A person carrying weight with too little coming back goes scattered — that's the body's honest math.

The exit isn't more effort. Rest doesn't do it, and forcing steadiness doesn't either. What fills this is being met. Let someone sit with you inside something hard, without you arranging it or tidying it up. You don't have to explain, or take advice, or hold yourself together for them. Something small and real comes of it: you're not alone under the load. That's what gathers you back.
cells.sheetLine: You've been holding it alone, and it's come apart.

cells.tense: The pen is down while you are standing in a room you're already writing.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Take a thing you keep doing with other people — a weekly call, a standing meal — and change one detail of it this time. Say the change out loud so it sticks.
cells.core:
You keep the whole thing steady, and your own account says you're just getting through it. The adjusting happens — you feel when to press and when to give — and you don't count it as a choice. When anyone asks how things stay even, you point at the situation, not your hand inside it.

What's invisible to you is that you've been shaping it. Something you keep with other people runs on your quiet upkeep, and that upkeep has kept it alive and breathing. Change one thing about it on purpose this time. Say the change out loud so it lands as a decision rather than a drift. What's been maintained by feel turns out to be written by you, and that was true the whole way.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping the ritual alive and calling it nothing.

attempts.check: The record supports the card's mechanism (Tune, dynamic equilibrium, Cognition channel) and the seat's capacity (Fortitude, holding under pressure) but does not state this person's particular history of balance or fragmentation — the Too Much cell risks overclaiming that the person routinely performs ease they don't have before others, and the Too Little cell risks asserting a specific loss or injury that the record never names. A reader could reasonably say the pattern is situational rather than chronic. The asks survive being wrong: each one is small, observable, and useful even if the diagnosis of status is off, because they teach the person something about their own calibration either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any version of 'you've always been the steady one' — cut it.
